results.title: Drive Duet Transport Chair Review: A Versatile Walker and Transport Chair
results.text:
Skip to content

SeniorsMobility is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Learn more

 By jwilder

The Drive Medical Duet Transport Chair/Rollator Walker is one of the most unique mobility aids on the market. It’s got one-of-a-kind dual functionality; no other Drive model can safely be a rollator walker and a transport chair! This is a versatile comfortable chair that is perfect for those who need a mobility aid to improve their balance, lessen pain, and retain their independence and physical wellness.

Read our Drive Duet Transport Chair review below to see if this model is right for you!

Review of: Drive Duet Transport Chair

Please click image for more info

What We Like:

- Dual functions
- Relatively light
- No tool assembly

What We Don’t Like:

- Slow
- Not for tall users

Our Conclusion: The Drive Medical Duet Transport Chair/Rollator Walker is perfect for the needs of just about any senior. It’s lightweight and perfect for indoor and outdoor use. However, no feature is more impressive than the ability to quickly turn the rollator into a safe, stable transport chair! 

## Features of Drive Duet Transport Chair

### Two Chairs in One

Make no mistake, this is the best feature of the Drive Duet, and one of the best features in the entire rollator market! With just two simple steps, you can convert the Duet from a rollator walker into a transport chair/wheelchair! Normal rollators are only meant to be used as walkers or seats; being pushed by someone in a rollator is rather foolish. The Duet earns its name because it can easily become a wheelchair, so you can be pushed in both comfort and safety!

First, remove the backrest from the rollator (this happens with the touch of a button) and attach it to the other side. This is important not only for comfort while being pushed; it also keeps the two swiveling wheels in front no matter what mode of use! That adds stability and safety to the chair.

Second, flip open the footrest and armrests. These, too, are unlocked/locked in place with a button, so they’re very easy to use. Now, you’re ready to be pushed wherever you need to go! You won’t be able to push yourself as you would with a traditional wheelchair; that’s why the name “transport chair” is a bit more accurate.

This versatility is incredibly valuable; now, you don’t have to choose between a rollator or wheelchair. Nor do you need to have two different devices or switch between them; you can get one chair that does double duty. This saves you money, space, and headaches for years to come!

### 8-Inch Indoor/Outdoor Wheels

This is always a welcome feature on a rollator walker; it gives you more freedom over the places you’re able to go without risking a fall; rollators are the best mobility aid for avoiding falls while out and about. Taller wheels provide greater stability and impact absorption. When using the Duet in transport chair mode, this feature is even more helpful!

When you’re walking outdoors with the Duet, you can have confidence that you won’t be limited to just sidewalks and concrete. You can go just about anywhere you like! The entire purpose of a mobility aid is to help you retain your independence and freedom; large indoor/outdoor wheels go a long way to accomplishing that!

### Spacious Underseat Storage

Almost every rollator has a storage area under the seat, but they are often far too small. The Drive Duet transport chair/rollator walker has a zippered bag underneath the seat that will be able to store almost anything you need for the day!

Having a nice amount of under-seat storage isn’t just convenient- it helps keep you safe! Carrying things in your hands, over your shoulders, or in a backpack while using a rollator walker can be dangerous and lead to pulled muscles or falls.

### Easy Folding/Locking

The Drive Duet can fold up nearly flat, so you can store it in your home or car easily. It also locks in the open/folded positions easily, so you’ll never risk the chair collapsing while you’re walking or sitting in it. Most chairs that fold will lock into place when they’re open, but not when they’re folded shut. This model, however, will lock shut so that you also won’t have to worry about it expanding on you while you’re trying to lift it and put it in the car!

### Large Seat and High Weight Capacity

Neither the seat size nor the weight capacity of the Drive Duet is the best in the world, but they’re both worth mentioning. The standard seat size on most rollators- especially cheaper ones- is 10” X 10” or 10” X 12”. The seat on the Drive Duet is just a bit bigger: 13” X 13.5”. That, admittedly, isn’t a massive jump. However, it is significant enough that you’ll notice the difference in both comfort and stability while sitting!

The 300-pound weight capacity isn’t exactly anything to write home about either, but it is stronger than the average 250-pound limit of other rollators. Even if you’re not a particularly heavy person, it’s nice to have that kind of strength. It helps seniors feel more stable and secure in their rollators, giving them the confidence to safely go anywhere!

## Specifications of Drive Duet Transport Chair

- Back Height: 35″
- Shipping Weight: 25 lbs.
- Handle Height: 31.5″ – 37″
- Overall Dimensions: 25.5″ (W) x 37″ (H) x 26″ (L)
- Seat Dimensions: 13.5″ (W) x 13″ (D)
- Seat To Floor Height: 21″
- Seat Width: 13.5″
- Seat Width: 13.5″
- Weight: 20 lbs
- Weight: 20 lbs

## Video Overview of Drive Duet Transport Chair

## Pros and Cons of Drive Duet Transport Chair

PROS

- Dual Functions: Make no mistake, this is the absolute best feature of this rollator. In just a few minutes, your rollator can turn into a functioning transport chair. This versatility is virtually impossible to beat!
- Relatively Light: Some rollators weigh less, but 20 pounds is certainly on the lighter side. Couple that with the 8-inch wheels, and you’ve got a walker that is easy for anyone to maneuver and push!
- No-Tool Assembly: Right out of the box, the Drive Duet is almost ready to go. Just insert the handlebars and backrest (they’ll click into position), and your rollator/transport chair is completely assembled!

CONS

- Must be Slow When Using as Transport Chair: The Drive Duet, when it’s used as a transport chair/wheelchair, is pretty good. The only drawback is that you must push or be pushed slowly. Walking too fast means that any bumps in the pavement could result in the person being tipped out of the chair. It just isn’t as stable as a full-sized wheelchair, but it’s perfectly safe if you take your time!
- Not Suitable for Taller Users: This rollator’s handlebars extend up to a height of 37 inches. This means it can be used by anyone up to about 6’2”; if you’re taller, you may find it uncomfortable to use this rollator.

## Who the Drive Duet Transport Chair is Best For?

This rollator walker is perfect for people who are getting older and have limited mobility, as well as people who need a mobility aid for recovery or rehabilitation. It doesn’t function much differently than any other rollator; it’s easy to push, stable, and lightweight.

But, seniors who are reaching that 75+ age range will likely benefit greatly from being able to be pushed when they need it. Rollator walkers are great mobility aids, but when you are tired, sore, or otherwise more limited than you would normally be, it’s nice to have the transport chair option.

Likewise, people who are recovering/rehabilitating from surgery or injury will love being able to use both modes of the Drive Duet. It’s much better than having to purchase and use two separate devices!

## Other Mobility Aids to Consider

Curious about what else is out there? There are many great rollators in a similar price range, with similar features. Keep in mind, though, that the Drive Duet is one-of-a-kind in terms of dual functionality; no other rollator can safely be used as a transport chair!

### 1. Medline Empower Rollator Walker

The Empower is one of the most comfortable and versatile rollators on the market. It’s perfect for people who need to rest often, such as those with COPD, sciatic pain, and seniors with joint issues.

It’s lightweight and the seat/backrest is very plush. If you’re looking for a rollator you can take on long trips with superior comfort, the Empower is for you!

### **** 2. Medline Ultralight Transport Chair

If you’re thinking that a transport chair might serve your needs better than a rollator, this convenient model might be perfect for you! Similar to the Drive Duet, it’s got a high weight capacity, it’s easy to fold, and it weighs less than 15 pounds!

It’s also got desk-length armrests, making it convenient for use at work and the dinner table.

### **** 3. Drive Medical Four-Wheel Walker

This model from Drive Medical is extremely basic; it’s well-suited for temporary needs or just the person who doesn’t like to have anything fancy. It’s versatile and easy to use, but the real advantage is that it costs one-third the amount that other rollators do!

If you’re looking for something simple and affordable, this is a quality option you should consider!

## Conclusion: Drive Duet Transport Chair

This is an ideal mobility aid for recovery, rehabilitation, and daily use- anyone can benefit from the Drive Duet. If you’re looking for a versatile and helpful mobility aid, this could be it!

The Drive Duet Transport Chair Rollator Review – erollator.com

# The Drive Duet Transport Chair Rollator Review

My MS has progressed to the point that I don’t go out in public without walking assistance. With Multiple Sclerosis some days I need a walker and others a wheelchair; everyday is an adventure! Some days I can walk at least short distances and others I need to be pushed around! You can imagine my relief when I found The Drive Duet Transport Chair Rollator! Every time I am using my rollator, either by walking or sitting, someone comments!

When I am shopping, I can walk around the store, stop and sit until I’m recharged and strong enough to walk again.

If I’m getting pushed, this transport chair also features a comfortable footrest that folds down when being used as a wheel chair or folds up and out of the way when being used as a walker.

The Drive Duet Transport Chair Rollator is one of the first products to combine a walker and wheel chair into one easy to use mobility device. It only weighs about 19 pounds and is one of the few transport chairs that folds up so it’s easy to get into the trunk or the back seat of the car or fit alongside a bed when not in use.

The Duet features a comfortable, contoured back rest that has two adjustable positions that can be attached to the front or back providing maximum user comfort.

There is also a seat lock on The Duet Transport Chair Rollator that prevents the duet from accidentally folding up when in use or unfolding when being removed from the trunk. The comfortable padded seat even lifts up, providing easy access to the large carrying pouch and so no space is wasted.

The large 8 casters (wheels) provide a smooth ride over any surface whether you are being pushed or using the walker. I have found that when crossing the threshold of doors in public buildings, the ‚driver‘ of this wheel chair often needs to back in to get over the bump.

Duet Transport Chair Rollator weighs 19 lbs so it’s not too heavy to lift into the trunk. When the Rollator is open it’s about 25.5 inches wide and 37 inches high.

I have honestly been able to keep my mobility with the convenience of this walker that converts into a wheel chair! I have been able to travel all over the country alone. I fly with airlines who provide assistance to push me to the proper gate, where I can walk around until departure time. When I’m ready to board the plane I turn the walker around, sit, flip the footrest down the handles up and sit comfortably until the assistant is ready to push me to the plane entrance.

Like I said, I don’t get pushed around in public without people commenting! I decided to become an affiliate for The Drive Duet Transport Chair Rollator. When you buy it from my site, MSrelief.com, I’ll receive a small commission for your purchase at no extra cost to you. Knowing the satisfaction you’ll receive from this purchase warms my heart

Find your joy,

Linda

Linda Grace Cox I am a happily married mother of 8 with 6 grandchildren. I love helping others find joy while living with Multiple Sclerosis and other chronic conditions.

## At a glance

#### Highlights

- Combines the features of a Rollator and transport chair in one unit
- Locking flip-up armrests and flip-down footrest are used in transport chair mode and are easily removed and stowed away in Rollator mode
- Tool-free, two-position contoured padded backrest

- Folding frame with lock-out feature to ensure the unit stays open while in use and ensures the unit will stay folded during transport

#### Description

Experience the convenience and value of two outstanding products in a single safe, convenient aid to improving daily mobility with the Duet Rollator/Transport Chair from Drive Medical. As a Rollator, the Duet surpasses a standard walker by eliminating the need to lift the device and allowing you to walk with an easy, smooth gait. It handles uneven, outdoor terrain with ease and provides a comfortable and convenient place to rest with its cushioned seat. But the Duet is also a transport chair, making it great for being escorted around your home, or around the shopping mall. Simply lift the armrests, shift the backrest and lower the footrest into place, and your Duet is now a comfortable seat for you while a caregiver easily pushes you.

#### Love my Duet!!

I have used my duet quite a lot as both a walker and transport chair. It's been a life saver on 2 cruises with excursions, airplanes 8 times, of course left at the door of the plane to be placed below during the flights, weddings, a funeral and in and out of our cars about a million times. When I am feeling well enough to drive, I am able to slide it in and out of my trunk alone, as long as I can sit on my bumper! Very easy fold/unfold and secure lock in both positions. Like other reviewers, i would love to see a cushioned seat and larger, shock absorbing wheels as being a rider over bumpy terrain, like brick walkways, can be jarring. Going through doorways with any sort of threshold or the many seams in a ships construction, must be navigated backward for ease and safety. 6 Best Rollator Walkers in 2026 | ConsumerAffairs®

# Best Rollator Walkers 

 Updated Jul. 31, 2024 Fact-Checked 

 By: Anne Mercer 

 +1 more 

 Edited by: Justin Martino 

 Contents 

When shopping for a rollator, there are a few factors to consider: the weight capacity of the seat, any desired storage features and your budget — rollators range from $50 to a few hundred dollars or more. Also, check the total weight of the item to ensure it’s easy for you or a caregiver to transport. To select our top rollator picks, we considered these factors, ruled out any products with poor customer reviews and gave preference to rollators with built-in back support and storage features.

- Drive Duet Transport Rollator
- Drive Medical Adjustable Height
- Drive Aluminum Rollator
- ProBasics Aluminum Rollator
- Medline Basic Steel Rollator
- Medline Bariatric Heavy Duty Rollator

Our editorial standards

- Our editorial team reviews and fact-checks all content before it’s published.
- We rely on expert input and trusted sources to verify our articles.
- All articles published must meet our editorial standards and independence policy.

Our review standards

- Our moderation team evaluates reviews to make sure they meet our guidelines.
- We require contact information to verify reviews come from real customers.
- Financial relationships do not influence whether we publish a consumer review.

## Our top rollator walker picks 

### Drive Duet Transport Chair and Rollator

Product weight 20 pounds Weight capacity 300 pounds Adjustable Yes Back support Yes

 Overview 

This model features a padded, fold-up seat and a spacious underseat pouch for storing belongings. The design allows for indoor and outdoor use and includes a flip-down footrest for use while sitting. This feature effectively transforms the rollator into a transport chair, giving users the best of both worlds.

 Why we picked it 

The combination rollator transport chair functionality makes this pick a great value for your money. We also like that it comes in your choice of red, blue or black frame. Many rollators come in only red or blue, so the black option is a nice addition. This model also features locking, flip-up armrests for use while seated, which adds an extra layer of comfort and support.

 What to consider 

At $150.38 (at the time of publishing), this rollator is one of the pricier models on our list. You can definitely find a cheaper option if cost is a core concern.

 What people say 

Customer reviews mention that it’s easy to use and well made. While some reviewers say the rollator function works smoother than the transport chair function, the overall reviews for the product are overwhelmingly positive with a 4.3 star rating and more than 4,000 reviews on Amazon at the time of publication.

 Specifications 

- Seat width: 13.5”
- Seat height: 21”
- Handle height: 31.5” to 37”

### Drive Medical Adjustable Height Rollator

Product weight 16.7 pounds Weight capacity 300 pounds Adjustable Yes Back support Yes

 Overview 

The Drive medical adjustable height rollator comes with 6-inch wheels, a removable padded backrest and soft grip tires for indoor and outdoor use. The padded seat also includes a zippered underseat pouch for personal items. Loop locks also provide extra stability and security when mobile.

 Why we picked it 

This model features offset casters that provide additional strength. Both the seat and the handles can be adjusted to suit the height of the user. The seat adjusts from 18 inches to 22 inches, while the handle height can adjust from 29.5 inches to 38 inches.

 What to consider 

Without a locking mechanism for the folded device, some users reported trouble with it staying closed and flat during transport, especially when moving it in and out of vehicles. This may not be an issue if you’re not planning on transporting the walker often. If you are, getting a cheap piece of velcro or bungee cord to secure the rollator during transportation may solve the problem.

 What people say 

Most users agreed that the rollator was easy to assemble, fold and use. Some customers noted that the seat height adjustment made this rollator a good choice for shorter individuals, with a few users ranging in height from 4 feet, 11 inches to 5 feet, 2 inches chiming in that the rollator adjusted to suit them well.

 Specifications 

- Seat height: adjustable 18” to 22”
- Handle height: 29.5” to 38”

### Drive Aluminum Rollator

Product weight 14 pounds Weight capacity 300 pounds Adjustable Yes Back support Yes

The easy-to-use Drive aluminum rollator features a removable padded backrest and ergonomic handles. Adjust the height to your desired level, up to 38 inches, and enjoy comfortable support when walking or resting. Storage features include a zippered underseat pouch.

 Why we picked it 

At 7.5 inches, the wheels are among the largest on our list. Typically speaking, the larger the wheel, the smoother your walking experience will be, which makes this a good option for anyone who knows their rollator is going to get heavy use and/or outdoor use.

The quality of wheels should make it easy to use on any terrain, including indoors on hardwood and carpet alike. Just be sure to check the specifications to see if it will clear all the door frames in your home.

 What people say 

Customers praise the price for the value and note the rollator is durable and sturdy and appears to be well made. At around 14 pounds, many users found it easy to lift and transport themselves, while a few others found it a bit too heavy to handle on their own when lifting it into or out of a vehicle.

 Specifications 

- Seat width: Not stated
- Seat height: Not stated
- Handle height: 33” to 38”

### ProBasics Aluminum Rollator

Product weight 13 pounds Weight capacity 300 pounds Adjustable Yes Back support Yes

Built from lightweight aluminum, the ProBasics aluminum rollator features 6-inch wheels and provides support, stability and maneuverability. The rollator has ergonomic hand brakes, a flip-up padded seat and a removable padded backrest. Storage features include an attachable water-resistant nylon pouch.

 Why we picked it 

At 13 pounds, this is the lightest rollator on our list. We like this option for anyone who may need to lift the walker in and out of a vehicle themselves. If look and design is important to you, this rollator comes in four color options, the most of any on our list. Options include red, black or two shades of blue.

The seat height does not appear to be adjustable, but the handle height is. Be sure to look at the specifications to make sure the seat height will suit you.

 What people say 

Customers commented on the easy assembly and folding function. The light weight makes it easy to transport, though some users reported they had to place it in their backseat because it was too big for their trunk. If you’re concerned, be sure to check the measurements of the rollator beside the measurements for your vehicle before purchase.

 Specifications 

- Seat width: 14”
- Seat height: 23”
- Handle height: 32” to 37”

### Medline Basic Steel Rollator

Product weight 19 pounds Weight capacity 350 pounds Adjustable Yes Back support No

The Medline Basic rollator’s powder-coated steel frame makes it a lightweight and durable choice. The rollator folds compactly for storage and includes a padded seat. This model also includes underseat storage and supports weights up to 350 pounds.

 Why we picked it 

As the cheapest rollator on our list, we like the affordability factor for the user. In addition to the low price, this rollator also has one of the highest weight capacities of any on our list at 350 pounds — this is about as high as we’ve seen on a nonbariatric model. We like the durability and support the rollator provides to all sizes.

The handle height adjusts from 31 inches to 35 inches. While this is likely to serve many users, it is a lower adjustable range than most of the rollators on our list, which tend to adjust from 31 inches up to 38 inches. If you’re a taller individual, make sure this height works for you.

 What people say 

Customers like the price and ease of assembly, with one customer estimating it took fewer than five minutes to put together. Some customers did comment on the handle height, estimating it might not be high enough for users taller than 5 feet, 7 inches.

- Seat width: 12”
- Seat height: 20.5”
- Handle height: 31” to 35”

### Medline Bariatric Heavy Duty Steel Rollator

Product weight 25 pounds Weight capacity 500 pounds Adjustable Yes Back support Yes

The Medline Bariatric Heavy Duty Steel Rollator can support up to 500 pounds. It also includes easy-to-use loop breaks, a padded seat and removable padded backrest. The rollator has underseat storage.

While a little pricier, this rollator is built to support weights up to 500 pounds and features 8-inch wheels for easy terrain navigation. For extra support, the rollator features a reinforced steel frame.

With greater weight capacity comes a greater total device weight. At 25 pounds, this is the heaviest rollator on our list and may be difficult for an individual with mobility issues to lift and transport on their own.

Most customers comment that the piece is well built and easy to assemble. Some customers have had issues with wheel stability and quality.

- Seat width: 17.5”
- Seat height: 22”
- Handle height: 31.5" to 37.5"

## Ultimate guide to buying rollator walkers 

Rollator walkers are a great option for those who need assistance walking and want the ability to take breaks easily. They come in different sizes, with adjustable heights, and some can fold down for storage. Read on to get a better understanding of what you need to look for in a rollator walker.

## Key insights

Rollator walkers are different from traditional walkers because they have more wheels and a seat.
